1.q: At the hawker centre, Uncle puts 4 satay sticks on each of 3 plates. Then he adds 2 more sticks. How many sticks are there now?
1.hint: Add the sticks on the 3 plates first, then the extra ones.
1.why: 3 plates of 4 sticks make 12 sticks. Add the 2 more: 14 sticks.

1.q: Wei Jie looks at the house numbers from 1 to 40 on his lane. He circles each number that ends in 3 or 7. How many numbers does he circle?
1.hint: Look at the ones digit only.
1.why: The numbers are 3, 7, 13, 17, 23, 27, 33 and 37. That is 8 numbers.

1.q: A ribbon is 96 cm long. Mum cuts it into 3 pieces of the same length. How long is each piece?
1.hint: Share the length into equal pieces. Which number times 3 makes 96?
1.why: 3 pieces of 32 cm each: 32 + 32 + 32 = 96, so each piece is 32 cm long.

1.q: The lift in Kumar's HDB block is on floor 6. It goes up 4, then down 5, then up 2. Which floor is the lift on now?
1.hint: Start at floor 6. Count up or down on a number line.
1.why: The floors in order are 6, 10, 5, 7. The lift ends on floor 7.

1.q: Kumar's swimming lesson is in 4 days. Today is Wednesday. On which day is the lesson?
1.hint: Count on one day at a time. Tomorrow is day 1.
1.why: Count on from Wednesday: Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. The lesson is on Sunday.

1.q: A tile has 6 sides. Every side is 3 cm long. An ant walks once all the way round the edge of the tile. How far does the ant walk?
1.hint: Add the side length once for every side.
1.why: Add the sides: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 18 cm.

1.q: Two bags hold 60 buns in all. One bag has 10 more buns than the other. How many buns are in the bigger bag?
1.hint: If the bags held the same, how many would each have? Then move some buns across.
1.why: The bigger bag has 35 buns and the smaller has 25. They add to 60 and differ by 10. The bigger bag has 35 buns.

1.q: The school bus leaves at 9 o'clock in the morning for a trip. The trip lasts 5 hours. At what o'clock does the trip end?
1.hint: Count on the hours on a clock face. After 12 comes 1.
1.why: Count on from 9 o'clock: 10, 11, 12, 1, 2. The trip ends at 2 o'clock.

1.q: Farhan has 3 T-shirts and 2 pairs of shorts. An outfit is one T-shirt and one pair of shorts. How many different outfits can he make?
1.hint: Pick one T-shirt. How many outfits does it make with the shorts?
1.why: Each of the 3 T-shirts goes with 2 pairs of shorts. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 outfits.

1.q: I think of a number. I double it, then I add 3. My answer is 25. What is my number?
1.hint: Work backwards. Undo the adding first, then undo the doubling.
1.why: Backwards: 25 − 3 = 22, and half of 22 is 11. Check: double 11 is 22, and 22 + 3 = 25.

1.q: A pond has 3 lily pads on Monday. Every day the number of lily pads doubles. How many lily pads does the pond have on Thursday?
1.hint: Doubling means two times as many. Write the number for each day.
1.why: Monday 3, then doubling each day: 3, 6, 12, 24. On Thursday there are 24 lily pads.

1.q: Aunty has 17 cupcakes. A box holds 4 cupcakes. How many boxes does she need to pack all the cupcakes?
1.hint: Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12 ... Is 16 enough?
1.why: 4 boxes hold 16 cupcakes. 1 cupcake is left over, and it needs another box. So she needs 5 boxes.

1.q: Siti has 14 stickers and Ben has 8 stickers. Siti passes some of her stickers to Ben, and then the two children have equal amounts. How many does Siti pass over?
1.hint: Find how many more stickers Siti has than Ben. Each sticker that Siti gives moves across the gap.
1.why: Siti has 6 more than Ben. Each sticker she gives makes the gap 2 smaller, so she gives half of 6, which is 3 stickers. Check: they both have 11.

1.q: Kaya toast costs $5 each. A cup of hot chocolate costs $3. Mum buys 2 toasts and 3 cups of hot chocolate. How much does she pay?
1.hint: Add the toasts first. Then add the cups of hot chocolate.
1.why: Kaya toast: 2 × $5 = $10. Hot chocolate: 3 × $3 = $9. Together that is $19.

1.q: Jun Hao uses lolly sticks to make a row of squares. One square uses 4 sticks. Two squares joined side by side use 7 sticks. How many sticks do 5 squares joined in a row use?
1.hint: A new square shares one side with the last square. How many new sticks does it need?
1.why: Each new square adds 3 sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13, 16. So 5 squares use 16 sticks.

1.q: Mei Ling starts reading at half past 3 and stops at 5 o'clock. For how many minutes does she read?
1.hint: Split the time at 4 o'clock. Count the minutes in each part.
1.why: Half past 3 to 4 o'clock is 30 minutes. 4 o'clock to 5 o'clock is 60 minutes. 30 + 60 = 90 minutes.

1.q: 5 friends meet at the void deck. Every friend gives a high five to each of the other friends, once. How many high fives are there?
1.hint: Call the friends A, B, C, D and E. List the pairs, such as AB.
1.why: A makes 4 high fives. B makes 3 more, C makes 2 more and D makes 1 more: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 high fives.

1.q: Hui Min writes this pattern: 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ... Each jump is 1 bigger than the jump before. What is the 7th number in her pattern?
1.hint: Write down the jumps: 1, then 2, then 3. Keep going and keep adding.
1.why: The jumps are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The numbers are 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, 22. The 7th number is 22.

1.q: A line of 9 children waits for the water cooler. Hui Min is 3rd from the front. Counting from the other end, which place is she in?
1.hint: Draw the line with dots. Mark Hui Min, then count the children behind her.
1.why: There are 9 children. The 3 children at the front, including Hui Min, are not behind her. So 9 − 3 + 1 = 7, and she is 7th from the back.

1.q: Mei Ling lists 2-digit numbers whose two digits are the same, such as 22 and 66. How many numbers can she list?
1.hint: Think about the tens digit first. It can be any digit from 1 to 9.
1.why: The numbers are 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88 and 99. That is 9 numbers.

1.q: Priya has three number cards: 7, 0 and 3. She puts every card side by side to make a 3-digit number. Which is the smallest number she could make?
1.hint: A 3-digit number cannot start with 0.
1.why: The first digit cannot be 0, so start with the smallest other card, 3. Then use 0, then 7. The number is 307.

1.q: Xin Yi threads beads in this pattern again and again: pink, green, green, pink, green, green, ... What colour is the 10th bead?
1.hint: Each pattern has 3 beads. The 3rd, 6th and 9th beads are green.
1.why: The pattern starts again after every 3 beads. The 9th bead ends a pattern, so the 10th bead starts a new one. It is pink.

1.q: In the school hall, the front row has 1 chair. The next row has 2 chairs, then 3, and so on up to 6 chairs in the last row. How many chairs are there altogether?
1.hint: Pair up the rows: the first with the last, the second with the one before last.
1.why: Pair the rows: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4. Each pair makes 7. 3 pairs make 21 chairs.

1.q: Jun Hao is taller than Mei Ling. Xin Yi is taller than Jun Hao. Who is the tallest?
1.hint: Draw three lines. Make the tallest person's line the longest.
1.why: Xin Yi is taller than Jun Hao, and Jun Hao is taller than Mei Ling. From tallest: Xin Yi, Jun Hao, Mei Ling. So Xin Yi is the tallest.

1.q: A bun costs $3 and a drink costs $2. Ben hands over $20. What change does the shopkeeper give back?
1.hint: Find the cost of the bun and the drink together first.
1.why: The bun and the drink cost $5 together. $20 take away $5 leaves $15.

1.q: A path goes round a pond and is 20 steps long. Aunty puts a pot of flowers every 4 steps, all the way round. How many pots does she need?
1.hint: Draw a circle. Mark a pot every 4 steps. Do not count the starting pot twice.
1.why: 20 steps ÷ 4 steps = 5 pots. Because the path is a loop, the last pot is next to the first one.

1.q: Hui Min pays exactly 30 cents using 10-cent coins and 5-cent coins. She may use only one kind of coin if she likes. How many different sets of coins can she use?
1.hint: Start with no 10-cent coins. How many 5-cent coins make 30 cents? Then try one 10-cent coin.
1.why: With no 10-cent coin: six 5-cent coins. With one 10-cent coin: four 5-cent coins. With two: two 5-cent coins. With three: none. That is 4 sets.

1.q: A string has 50 beads. 12 are red and 7 are blue. The rest are yellow. How many beads are yellow?
1.hint: Add the red and blue beads first. Then see how many more make 50.
1.why: Red and blue beads: 19. 50 take away 19 leaves 31 beads.

1.q: In a star graph, each star stands for 10 children. The swimming row has 5 stars and the badminton row has 2 stars. How many more children chose swimming than badminton?
1.hint: First find how many more stars the swimming row has. Then think about what each star is worth.
1.why: Swimming has 3 more stars. Each star is worth 10 children, so 3 stars are 3 × 10, which is 30 children.

1.q: Aisha's art camp starts on the 9th and ends on the 15th. The first day and the last day both count as camp days. How many days is the camp?
1.hint: Write down every date from the first day to the last day. Then count them.
1.why: Count every date from the 9th to the 15th, both included: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 7 days.

2.q: Kumar visits a farm and counts 5 hens and 3 goats. Every hen stands on 2 legs and every goat on 4 legs. What is the total number of legs?
2.hint: Work out the hens' legs and the goats' legs separately. Then add.
2.why: 5 × 2 = 10 and 3 × 4 = 12. 10 + 12 = 22 legs. Altogether there are 22 legs.

2.q: Sam makes a row of triangles with lolly sticks. One triangle uses 3 sticks. Two triangles joined side by side use 5 sticks. How many sticks do 8 triangles in a row use?
2.hint: Each new triangle shares one side. How many new sticks does it need?
2.why: Each new triangle adds 2 sticks: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17. So 8 triangles use 17 sticks.

2.q: A tray has 6 rows with 5 egg tarts in each row. Then 4 tarts are eaten. How many tarts are left on the tray?
2.hint: Find how many tarts there are before any are eaten.
2.why: 6 rows of 5 make 30 tarts. 30 − 4 = 26 tarts.

2.q: 4 rice cakes cost $5.20. Mum buys 7 rice cakes at the same price each. How much does she pay?
2.hint: Find the price of 1 rice cake first.
2.why: 1 rice cake costs $1.30. 7 rice cakes cost 7 × $1.30 = $9.10.

2.q: Aisha is older than Ben. Priya is older than Kumar. Kumar is older than Aisha. Who is younger than Priya but older than Aisha?
2.hint: Put the four names in a row from oldest to youngest.
2.why: From oldest to youngest: Priya, Kumar, Aisha, Ben. Kumar is younger than Priya and older than Aisha.

2.q: 7 friends are in a table-tennis club. Each friend plays one game against every other friend. How many games are played?
2.hint: Each friend plays 7 − 1 games, but each game has two players.
2.why: Each of the 7 friends plays 6 games, which makes 42. Each game was counted twice, so 42 ÷ 2 = 21 games.

2.q: In one month, the 1st is a Tuesday. What is the date of the 3rd Saturday in that month?
2.hint: Find the first Saturday of the month. Then add 7 for each next one.
2.why: The first Saturday is the 5th. Adding 7 each time gives the 5th, 12th and 19th. The 3rd Saturday is the 19th.

2.q: On a star graph, each star stands for 5 books. Class A has 16 stars and Class B has 6 stars. How many more books did Class A read than Class B?
2.hint: Find how many more stars Class A has. Then count each star as 5 books.
2.why: Class A has 10 more stars. Each star is 5 books, so 10 × 5 = 50 books.

2.q: Siti's poster is a rectangle 12 cm long and 7 cm wide. She sticks a gold ribbon all the way round the edge. How long is the ribbon?
2.hint: A rectangle has two long sides and two short sides.

2.q: A snail climbs a 20 cm wall. Each day it climbs 5 cm. Each night it slides back 2 cm. On which day does it first reach the top?
2.hint: Draw the wall. Mark where the snail is at the end of each day and at the end of each night.
2.why: At the end of each day it is at 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20 cm (it slides back 2 cm each night). It reaches 20 cm on day 6, so it never slides back from the top.

2.q: How many faces do a cube and a square pyramid have altogether? A square pyramid has a square base and four triangle faces.
2.hint: Count the faces of each solid separately. Then add.
2.why: a cube has 6 faces and a square pyramid has 5 faces. Altogether that is 11 faces.

2.q: A floor plan is 7 squares across and 5 squares down. A corner that is 3 squares across and 2 squares down is cut out for a stairwell. How many squares are left in the plan?
2.hint: Count all the squares in the big rectangle first. Then take away the squares that are cut out.
2.why: The whole rectangle has 35 squares. The corner that is cut out has 6 squares. 35 − 6 = 29 squares.

2.q: In a class of 30 children, 18 have a pet dog and 15 have a pet cat. 4 children have no pet at all. How many children have both a dog and a cat?
2.hint: Find how many children have at least one pet. Add the dog owners and cat owners and compare.
2.why: 26 children have at least one pet. 18 + 15 = 33, and 33 is 7 more than 26. Those 7 were counted twice, so 7 children have both.

2.q: A necklace has this pattern again and again: red, yellow, yellow, blue, red, yellow, yellow, blue, ... It has 68 beads. How many beads are yellow?
2.hint: How many beads are in one pattern? How many patterns fit into 68 beads?
2.why: One pattern has 4 beads and 2 of them are yellow. 68 ÷ 4 = 17 patterns, so 17 × 2 = 34 yellow beads.

2.q: A small jug fills 3 cups. A big jug fills 5 small jugs. Hui Min has 2 big jugs of barley water. How many cups can she fill?
2.hint: Work out how many cups one big jug fills.
2.why: One big jug fills 5 small jugs, and each small jug fills 3 cups: 5 × 3 = 15 cups. Two big jugs fill 2 × 15 = 30 cups.

2.q: Hui Min pays exactly 30 cents using 20-cent, 10-cent and 5-cent coins. She may leave out a kind of coin if she likes. How many different sets of coins can she use?
2.hint: Count by the number of 20-cent coins she uses: none, or one.
2.why: With no 20-cent coin, 30 cents is 10-cent and 5-cent coins: 4 ways. With one 20-cent coin, 10 cents are left: 2 ways. 4 + 2 = 6 sets.

2.q: A secret 3-digit number has three clues. Its tens digit is 3. Its hundreds digit is 2 more than its tens digit. Its units digit is double its tens digit. What is the secret number?
2.hint: Start with the tens digit, because it is given.
2.why: Tens digit: 3. Hundreds digit: 3 + 2 = 5. Units digit: 3 × 2 = 6. I am 536.

2.q: A shop has 3 boxes of 100 pens, 15 packs of 10 pens and 8 single pens. How many pens does the shop have?
2.hint: 15 packs of 10 is more than 100. Count the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.
2.why: 3 boxes is 300 pens. 15 packs is 150 pens. 300 + 150 + 8 = 458 pens.

2.q: A bean plant has 2 leaves in week 1. The number of leaves doubles every week. How many leaves does the plant have in week 5?
2.hint: Write the number of leaves for each week. Double the last number each time.
2.why: Week 1 has 2. Doubling each week gives 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Week 5 has 32 leaves.

2.q: Two cups of bubble tea cost $4.80 each. Priya pays $20. How much change does she get?
2.hint: Find the cost of 2 cups first. Then take it away from the money she pays.
2.why: 2 cups cost $9.60. $20 take away $9.60 leaves $10.40.

2.q: Today is Tuesday. Mei Ling's class trip is in 20 days. On which day of the week is the trip?
2.hint: A week has 7 days, so the same day comes round every 7 days.
2.why: 20 days is 2 weeks and 6 days. Two weeks later it is Tuesday again. Then 6 more days: Monday.

2.q: The lift starts on floor 12. It goes down 5, then up 8, then down 9, then up 3. What is the highest floor the lift reaches?
2.hint: Write down the floor after each move. Then find the biggest.
2.why: The floors in order are 12, 7, 15, 6, 9. The highest is 15.

2.q: A path goes right round a pond. The path is 24 m long. A lamp post stands every 3 m, all the way round. How many lamp posts are there?
2.hint: The path is a loop. Does the last post need a different one at the start?
2.why: On a loop, the posts are shared out in equal gaps: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 lamp posts. There is no extra post because the end is the start.

2.q: Mei Ling and her brother have 90 stickers together. Mei Ling has 14 more stickers than her brother. How many stickers does Mei Ling have?
2.hint: Take away the 14 extra stickers. Share what is left equally. Then put the 14 back.
2.why: Without the extra 14, there are 76 stickers. Half is 38, which is her brother's share. Mei Ling has 38 + 14 = 52 stickers.

2.q: In Wei Jie's sticker book, page 1 has 2 stickers, page 2 has 4 and page 3 has 6. This goes up by 2 each page. Page 10 has 20 stickers. How many stickers are on all 10 pages?
2.hint: Pair the first page with the last, the second with the one before last.
2.why: Pairs: 2 + 20, 4 + 18, 6 + 16, 8 + 14, 10 + 12. Each pair is 22. 5 pairs make 110 stickers.

2.q: Aisha bakes 36 egg tarts. She gives 1/4 of them to her neighbours. How many egg tarts does she give away?
2.hint: Share 36 into 4 equal groups. One group is 1/4.
2.why: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. One quarter is 9 egg tarts.

2.q: A dessert stall has 3 ice-cream flavours, 2 kinds of cone and 2 toppings. A dessert is one flavour, one cone and one topping. How many different desserts can you make?
2.hint: Pick a flavour. How many cone and topping choices go with it?
2.why: 3 × 2 × 2 = 12 desserts.

2.q: 5 children share 29 buns, and each child takes as many buns as possible. How many buns will not be shared out?
2.hint: Count in 5s until you get close to 29.
2.why: Each child gets 5 buns. That uses 5 × 5 = 25 buns. 29 − 25 = 4 buns are left over.

2.q: The class assembly begins at 9:40 and finishes at 10:35. For how many minutes does it run?
2.hint: From 9:40 to 10:00 is how many minutes? Then add the rest.
2.why: From 9:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes. From 10:00 to 10:35 is 35 minutes. 20 + 35 = 55 minutes.

2.q: A baker puts the same number of buns in each of 3 boxes. A customer takes 4 buns out of the boxes. 23 buns are left. How many buns were in each box at first?
2.hint: Work backwards. Put the buns that were taken back first. Then share them among the boxes.
2.why: Put the 4 buns back: 23 + 4 = 27. Share 27 buns among 3 boxes: 27 ÷ 3 = 9 buns in each box.

3.q: Jun Hao draws a grid of small squares, 3 squares across and 3 squares down. He counts every square he can find, big and small. How many squares are there altogether?
3.hint: There are 9 small squares. Now look for bigger squares made of 4 small ones, then the biggest.
3.why: 9 small squares, 4 squares made of 2 by 2 small squares, and 1 big square made of 3 by 3 small squares. 9 + 4 + 1 = 14 squares.

3.q: Fill the 3 by 3 grid with the digits 1 to 9, using each digit one time. Every row, every column and both long diagonals must have the same total. Some digits are already placed, and ? shows an empty square. Which digit belongs in the bottom-right square?
3.hint: Add the top row first. That gives the total for every line.
3.why: The top row is 2 + 9 + 4 = 15, so every line adds to 15. Left column: 2 + 7 + 6, so the bottom-left is 6. Diagonal: 4 + 5 + 6, so the middle is 5. Middle row: 7 + 5 + 3, so the right of the middle row is 3. Right column: 4 + 3 + 8, so the bottom-right is 8.

3.q: Kuih costs $1.20 each. A cup of teh costs $1.80. Aisha buys 4 kuih and 2 cups of teh. She pays $10. How much change does she get?
3.hint: Find the cost of the kuih, then the cost of the teh. Add them. Then find the change.
3.why: 4 kuih cost $4.80 and 2 cups of teh cost $3.60. Together that is $8.40. $10 − $8.40 = $1.60.

3.q: Ali's father is 4 times as old as Ali. Together they are 45 years old. How old is Ali?
3.hint: Draw a bar for Ali and a bar 4 times as long for his father. How many equal parts are there in all?
3.why: Ali is 1 part and his father is 4 parts. Together that is 5 equal parts: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 years. Check: his father is 36.

3.q: A night bus leaves at 22:45 and arrives at 01:20 the next morning. How many minutes is the journey?
3.hint: Count the time from 22:45 to midnight. Then add the time from midnight to 01:20.
3.why: From 22:45 to midnight is 75 minutes. From midnight to 01:20 is 80 minutes. 75 + 80 = 155 minutes.

3.q: Mrs Lim puts the same number of eggs on each of 6 trays. She also has 9 loose eggs. She has 75 eggs altogether. How many eggs are on each tray?
3.hint: Work backwards. Take away the loose eggs first. Then share what is left among the trays.
3.why: Take away the loose eggs: 75 − 9 = 66. Share 66 eggs among 6 trays: 66 ÷ 6 = 11 eggs on each tray.

3.q: Ravi has 53 pencils. He packs them in boxes of 8, using as many full boxes as he can. How many pencils are left over?
3.hint: Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24 ... Stop before you pass 53.
3.why: 6 × 8 = 48, and 53 − 48 = 5. 5 pencils are left over.

3.q: Three houses next to each other on one side of a road have consecutive numbers, like 21, 22, 23. The three numbers add up to 114. What is the smallest house number?
3.hint: The middle number is the average of the three numbers.
3.why: 114 ÷ 3 = 38 is the middle number. The numbers are 37, 38 and 39. The smallest is 37.

3.q: Priya is faster than Ben. Ben is faster than Siti. Ravi is faster than Priya. Who finished third?
3.hint: Write the four names in a row from the fastest to the slowest.
3.why: From fastest to slowest: Ravi, Priya, Ben, Siti. The third is Ben.

3.q: A rectangle measures 8 cm by 6 cm. A square corner 3 cm by 3 cm is cut off. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
3.hint: Draw the shape. Mark each side that is left. Does cutting the corner make the edge shorter or longer?
3.why: The cut takes away some of two sides, but adds two new sides of the same total length. So the distance round stays the same as the rectangle: 8 + 6 + 8 + 6 = 28 cm.

3.q: A shop rounds every price to the nearest 10 cents. A price that is exactly halfway rounds up. How many different whole-cent prices from 1 cent upwards round to 350 cents?
3.hint: A price is within 5 of a multiple of 10. Does a price exactly halfway go up or down?
3.why: Prices from 345 cents to 354 cents round to 350 cents, because 345 rounds up to 350 and 355 rounds up to 360. That is 10 prices.

3.q: Mei Ling climbs 5 steps at the MRT station. Each time she takes 1 step or 2 steps. In how many different ways can she climb all 5 steps?
3.hint: First find the ways for 1 step, 2 steps, 3 steps and 4 steps. Look for a pattern.
3.why: The ways for 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 steps are 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. Each number is the sum of the two before it. So 5 steps can be climbed in 8 ways.

3.q: A fruit basket holds 4 mangoes weighing 250 g each and 3 papayas weighing 400 g each. Find the combined mass of all the fruit in grams.
3.hint: Work out the mango mass and the papaya mass separately. Then add.

3.q: A robot starts at the top-left corner of a grid. It moves only 4 steps right and 2 steps down, in any order, to reach the bottom-right corner. How many different routes can it take?
3.hint: Write each route as a string of R for right and D for down. Look for a way to count them without missing any.
3.why: Each route has 4 R and 2 D in some order. Count the routes to each corner by adding the routes from the left and from above. The bottom-right corner gets 15 routes.

3.q: Aisha buys 6 mangoes for $9.60. How much would 9 mangoes cost at the same price for each?
3.hint: Find the cost of 1 mango first.
3.why: 1 mango costs $1.60. 9 mangoes cost 9 × $1.60 = $14.40.

3.q: Today is Friday. A parcel will arrive 100 days from today. On which day of the week will it arrive?
3.hint: 100 days is 14 weeks and some days. Weeks do not change the day name.
3.why: 14 weeks is 98 days, and the day name is the same after whole weeks. 2 more days after Friday: Saturday, then Sunday.

3.q: Aisha's bus ticket shows a 3-digit number. She likes tickets whose number looks the same when it is read from right to left, like 232. How many such 3-digit numbers are there?
3.hint: Look at the digit on the far left and the digit on the far right. How many choices do you have for the first digit? And for the middle digit?
3.why: The first digit can be 1 to 9 and the last digit must match it. The middle digit can be 0 to 9. 9 × 10 = 90 numbers.

3.q: Siti pays exactly 40 cents using 20-cent, 10-cent and 5-cent coins. She may leave out a kind of coin if she likes. How many different sets of coins can she use?
3.hint: Count by the number of 20-cent coins: none, one or two.
3.why: No 20-cent coin: the 10-cent coins can be 0 to 4, so 5 ways. One 20-cent coin: 20 cents left, 3 ways. Two 20-cent coins: 1 way. 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 sets.

3.q: A baker bakes 7 trays with 9 buns on each tray. 5 buns burn and are thrown away. How many buns are left?
3.hint: Use the 9 times table to find how many buns there were at first.

3.q: How many edges do a cube and a square pyramid have altogether? A square pyramid has a square base and four triangle faces.
3.hint: Count the edges of each solid separately. Then add.
3.why: Counting separately, a cube has 12 edges and a square pyramid has 8 edges. Altogether that is 20 edges.

3.q: Jun Hao uses lolly sticks to make a grid of small squares that is 4 squares across and 2 squares down. Each side of a small square is one stick. How many sticks does he need?
3.hint: Count the sticks that lie across, row by row. Then count the sticks that stand up.
3.why: Across: 2 + 1 = 3 rows of 4 sticks = 12. Up: 4 + 1 = 5 columns of 2 sticks = 10. 12 + 10 = 22 sticks.

3.q: A train leaves at 7:48 and arrives at 9:15. How many minutes is the journey?
3.hint: First count on to the next whole hour.
3.why: 7:48 to 8:00 is 12 minutes. 8:00 to 9:00 is 60 minutes. 9:00 to 9:15 is 15 minutes. 12 + 60 + 15 = 87 minutes.

3.q: Wei Jie has four digit cards: 3, 9, 0 and 6. He uses all four cards to make an even 4-digit number. What is the smallest even number he can make?
3.hint: An even number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, and a number with four digits cannot begin with a zero.
3.why: The first digit should be small but not 0, so start with 3. Compare numbers ending in 0 (3690) and ending in 6 (3096). The smallest is 3096.

3.q: Wei Jie wants to pay exactly 135 cents. He has many 5-cent, 10-cent, 20-cent, 50-cent and $1 coins. What is the fewest coins he needs?
3.hint: Use the biggest coin that fits first. Then see what is left to pay.
3.why: Use 100 + 20 + 10 + 5. That is 4 coins.

3.q: Hui Min has 56 stamps. 3/8 of her stamps are from Singapore. How many stamps are from Singapore?
3.hint: Find 1/8 of 56 first. Then take 3 of those parts.
3.why: 56 ÷ 8 = 7. 3 parts of 7 is 3 × 7 = 21 stamps.

3.q: The minute hand of a clock starts at the 2 and turns clockwise until it points at the 11. How many right angles has it turned through?
3.hint: A right angle is a quarter turn. The numbers 12, 3, 6 and 9 are a quarter turn apart.
3.why: From 2 to 11 the hand passes 9 numbers. A quarter turn is 3 numbers, so 9 ÷ 3 = 3 right angles.

3.q: A kopitiam sold 450 cups of coffee and tea one morning. It sold 86 more cups of coffee than tea. How many cups of coffee did it sell?
3.hint: Draw two bars. The coffee bar is longer by 86.
3.why: Take away the extra 86: 450 − 86 = 364. Share equally: 364 ÷ 2 = 182 cups of tea. Coffee is 182 + 86 = 268 cups.

3.q: Mei Ling eats 1/4 of a pizza and Ben eats 3/8 of the same pizza. What fraction of the pizza did they eat altogether?
3.hint: Change 1/4 into eighths so both fractions have the same bottom number.

3.q: Mei Ling, Ben and Aisha each say one thing about who has the classroom key. Mei Ling says: "Aisha has the key." Ben says: "I do not have the key." Aisha says: "I have the key." Only one of the three children is being truthful. Who has the key?
3.hint: Try each child as the one with the key. Count how many statements are true each time.
3.why: If Mei Ling has the key, only Ben's statement is true. If Ben has it, nobody tells the truth. If Aisha has it, all three statements are true. Only one statement is true when Mei Ling has it, so the answer is Mei Ling.

3.q: Five children read books during the school year. Mei Ling read 19, Ben read 8, Aisha read 38, Ravi read 24 and Siti read 15. How many more books did the child who read the most read than the child who read the least?
3.hint: Find the biggest number and the smallest number first.
3.why: The most is 38 and the least is 8. 38 − 8 = 30 books.

4.q: A square garden has sides of 15 m. Uncle fences all four sides, except for a 2 m opening where the gate will go. How long is the fence?
4.hint: Find the distance all the way round first. Then take away the gate.

4.q: Hui Min writes the page numbers from 1 to 200. How many of these numbers have the digit 5 somewhere in them?
4.hint: Count the numbers with a 5 in the ones place, then the tens place. Be careful about 55 and 155.
4.why: Ones digit 5: 20 numbers. Tens digit 5: 50 to 59 and 150 to 159, which is 20 numbers. 55 and 155 are in both lists, so take away 2: 20 + 20 − 2 = 38 numbers.

4.q: Aisha has read 2/5 of a storybook. She has 15 pages still to read. How many pages does the book have?
4.hint: If she has read 2 out of every 5 parts, how many parts are left?
4.why: 3 of the 5 equal parts are left, and they are 15 pages. 1 part is 5 pages. All 5 parts are 5 × 5 = 25 pages.

4.q: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 5 o'clock? Use the smaller angle.
4.hint: The 12 numbers are equally spaced round the clock, and a full turn is 360°. How many degrees is one number?
4.why: A full turn of 360° is shared by 12 numbers, so one number is 30°. At 5 o'clock the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand at 5. 5 × 30 = 150°.

4.q: Mrs Lim's age is 3 times her son's age. Their ages add up to 64 years. How old is her son?
4.hint: Draw one bar for the son and a bar 3 times as long for his mother. Count the equal parts.
4.why: The son is 1 part and his mother is 3 parts, so there are 4 equal parts. 64 ÷ 4 = 16 years. His mother is 48.

4.q: Kumar, Priya, Wei Jie and Siti each say one thing about who has the lost library card. Kumar says: "I do not have it." Priya says: "Siti has it." Wei Jie says: "Siti has it." Siti says: "Wei Jie has it." Exactly one of the four statements is false. Who has the library card?
4.hint: Try each child as the one with the card. Count how many statements are true each time. You need exactly 3 true.
4.why: If Siti has it: Kumar's statement is true, Priya's is true, Wei Jie's is true, and only Siti's is false. That is exactly 3 true. No other child gives exactly 3 true statements. The answer is Siti.

4.q: A robot moves from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner of a grid. It takes 3 steps right and 3 steps down, in any order. It must avoid one point, which has a puddle, after 1 step right and 1 step down. How many routes can it take?
4.hint: First count all routes with no puddle. Then take away the routes that go through the puddle.
4.why: All routes: 20. Routes through the puddle point: 2 ways to get there × 6 ways to go on = 12. 20 − 12 = 8 routes.

4.q: Ben buys 3 story books. Each book costs $12.80. He pays $50. How much change does he get?
4.hint: Work out the cost of 3 books first.

4.q: The crowd at a football match was 47,562. What is this number rounded to the nearest thousand?
4.hint: Look at the hundreds digit. Is it 5 or more?
4.why: The hundreds digit is 5, so the thousands go up by one: 47,562 rounds to 48,000.

4.q: A line graph shows the height of a sunflower at the end of each week: 4 cm, 7 cm, 15 cm, 18 cm and 30 cm. What was the biggest growth in one week?
4.hint: Find how much the plant grew between each pair of neighbouring weeks.
4.why: The growth in each week was 3, 8, 3, 12. The biggest is 12 cm.

4.q: Each letter stands for a different digit. AB is a 2-digit number and CCB is a 3-digit number. AB × 3 = CCB. What digit is A?
4.hint: Look at the units digit. B × 3 ends in B. Which digit does that?
4.why: B × 3 ends in B only when B is 0 or 5. B = 0 fails, because A0 × 3 never starts with two matching digits. So B = 5, and 75 × 3 = 225 fits CCB. A is 7.

4.q: Priya has 96 chocolates and 72 sweets. She makes identical gift bags. No chocolates or sweets may be left over. What is the most bags she can make?
4.hint: The number of bags must divide 96 and 72 exactly. Try big numbers first.
4.why: The common factors of 96 and 72 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24. The greatest is 24 bags.

4.q: A farmer packs 2345 eggs into trays of 30, filling as many trays as he can. How many eggs are left over?
4.hint: Divide 2345 by 30. What is the remainder?
4.why: 78 × 30 = 2340, and 2345 − 2340 = 5. 5 eggs are left over.

4.q: Mr Tan puts 24 chairs in equal rows for a concert. Every row has the same number of chairs. How many different ways can he arrange them? (1 row of 24 counts as one way.)
4.hint: Find all pairs of numbers that multiply to 24.
4.why: The pairs are 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, 4 × 6, 6 × 4, 8 × 3, 12 × 2 and 24 × 1. Rows and chairs in a row swap, so there are 8 ways.

4.q: A tower has 20 rows of blocks. Row 1 has 3 blocks, row 2 has 6 blocks, row 3 has 9 blocks, and so on, going up by 3. Row 20 has 60 blocks. How many blocks are there in the whole tower?
4.hint: Pair the first row with the last row, the second with the one before last.
4.why: Each pair adds to 3 + 60 = 63. There are 10 pairs. 10 × 63 = 630 blocks.

4.q: Mei Ling uses 1.75 m of ribbon for a gift and 2.6 m of ribbon for a card. How many metres of ribbon does she use altogether?
4.hint: Line up the decimal points before you add.

4.q: A toy robot climbs a 30 cm ramp. Each minute it moves 7 cm up the ramp, then slips 4 cm back. After how many minutes does it first reach the top?
4.hint: Find the robot's height after the first minute. Then see how much it gains each minute after that.
4.why: At the top of minute 1 the robot is at 7 cm, then it slips to 3 cm. It gains 3 cm each minute, so at the top of minute k it is at 3k + 4 cm. The first k with 3k + 4 at least 30 is 9 minutes, because 3 × 9 + 4 = 31.

4.q: In the number 83,517, how much more is the value of the digit 8 than the value of the digit 5?
4.hint: The 8 is in the ten-thousands place and the 5 is in the hundreds place. Write the value of each.

4.q: In a school team list of 120 pupils, 70 play football and 65 play basketball. 20 pupils play neither game. How many pupils play both games?
4.hint: Find how many pupils play at least one game. Then add the two teams and compare.
4.why: 100 pupils play at least one game. 70 + 65 = 135, which is 35 more than 100. Those 35 were counted twice, so 35 pupils play both.

4.q: A film starts at 17:45 and ends at 20:10. How many minutes long is the film?
4.hint: 17:45 to 18:00 is 15 minutes. Then count on to 20:00 and then 20:10.
4.why: 17:45 to 18:00 is 15 minutes. 18:00 to 20:00 is 120 minutes. 20:00 to 20:10 is 10 minutes. 15 + 120 + 10 = 145 minutes.

4.q: Ben draws every line of symmetry on a square, an oblong rectangle with unequal sides, an equilateral triangle and an isosceles triangle with exactly two equal sides. How many lines does he draw altogether?
4.hint: A square and an equilateral triangle have as many lines of symmetry as they have sides. The rectangle is special.
4.why: Square 4, rectangle 2, equilateral triangle 3, isosceles triangle 1. 4 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 10 lines.

4.q: A rectangular garden measures 12 m by 8 m. One corner is a pond 4 m by 3 m, and the rest is grass. Find the area of the grass.
4.hint: Find the area of the whole garden. Then take away the area of the pond.

4.q: Siti draws a grid of small squares, 3 squares across and 3 squares down. She counts every rectangle she can find, including squares and big rectangles. How many rectangles are there?
4.hint: Count by width first: how many ways to pick a width of 1, 2 and 3 along one row?
4.why: Along one side, there are 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 ways to pick a width. Down the other side, also 6. 6 × 6 = 36 rectangles.

4.q: A jug holds 0.75 L of milk. Ben fills 6 jugs. How many litres of milk is that?
4.hint: Think of 0.75 as three quarters of a litre. Four jugs would make 3 litres.

4.q: Kumar types 7 + 6 × 4 − 9 into a calculator that follows the order of operations. What answer should it show?
4.hint: Do multiplication before addition and subtraction.

4.q: Find the smallest 5-digit number in which the five digits have a sum of 20.
4.hint: Keep the biggest digits at the end, because digits on the left are worth more. The first digit cannot be 0.
4.why: Start with 1 on the left. Then 0 and 1, and use two 9s at the end to reach 20: 1 + 0 + 1 + 9 + 9 = 20. The number is 10,199.

4.q: A recipe needs 2 3/4 cups of flour for a cake and 1 5/8 cups of flour for biscuits. How much flour is needed altogether? Give your answer as a mixed number.
4.hint: Change the fractions so they have the same bottom number.

4.q: Ali had some pencils. He gave 12 pencils to his brother. Then he shared all the pencils he had left equally among 5 friends, and each friend got 8 pencils. How many pencils did Ali have at first?
4.hint: Work backwards. Find how many pencils he shared out in all. Then put back the pencils he gave to his brother.
4.why: Shared out: 5 × 8 = 40 pencils. Put back the 12 from his brother: 40 + 12 = 52 pencils.

4.q: Four consecutive even numbers add up to 108. What is the smallest of the four numbers?
4.hint: Consecutive even numbers go up by 2: n, n + 2, n + 4, n + 6.
4.why: The four numbers are n, n + 2, n + 4 and n + 6, which add to 4n + 12. 4n + 12 = 108, so 4n = 96 and n = 24.

4.q: 7 runners take part in a race. The first runner wins gold, the second wins silver and the third wins bronze. In how many different ways can the three medals be given out?
4.hint: Choose the gold winner first. Then see how many runners are left for silver.
4.why: 7 choices for gold, then 6 for silver, then 5 for bronze. 7 × 6 × 5 = 210 ways.
